question: Can one bounded same-run resume recover a naturally timed-out Provider request without turning the three-repeat evaluation into task retry, and does the corrected autonomous CPS4-or-CPS4R Case pass its existing 2/3 gate?

decision.status: One naturally interrupted CodingRun resumed from its settled step history and then passed the complete licensed oracle, but the formal autonomous element-choice batch remained 1/3 and failed its 2/3 gate.
claims_allowed: The opt-in evaluator path performed a real same-run resume after a natural OpenCode Go ModelAPIError instead of creating a replacement evaluation task.
The recovered run preserved cumulative usage and later completed the licensed CAE, Solver, ODB extraction and host-oracle path.
One autonomous run selected 80 uniform CPS4 elements, asked no element question, and passed the corrected CPS4-or-CPS4R contract.
The other two runs each exhausted the single allowed resume and failed before files or Abaqus execution.
claims_forbidden: The autonomous element-choice profile passed its Product smoke gate.
Same-run resume guarantees recovery from Provider outages.
The 0/3 to 1/3 difference is caused by resume or HTTP retry settings.
Abaqus or Solver effects interrupted in flight were reconciled or resumed.

limits: The recovered interruption occurred after settled read-only capability/directory work and before the first Abaqus invocation; it does not test an in-flight external Job.
Only this plate evaluator exposes the explicit auto-resume flag; the ordinary CLI retains manual --resume as the general low-level mechanism.
Three attempts of one Case are a smoke gate, not a stable Provider or model success-rate estimate.
